children: Robusta coffee futures on ICE steadied off the prior session's three-year lows on Monday, with new crop arrivals in top grower Vietnam said to be relatively slow, while raw sugar also recovered.
COFFEE
* Robusta coffee
was little changed at $2,882 a metric ton at 1222 GMT, after setting a three-year low of $2,854 on Friday.
* Vietnam is currently harvesting what is set to be a bumper harvest and while weather conditions remain favourable, new crop arrivals are still relatively slow, said a Vietnam-based dealer.
* He also noted that farmers in the country face sharply higher picking costs.
* Elsewhere, ICE robusta exchange stocks were last at their lowest in more than a month (LRC-TOT-VG), helping put a floor under prices.
* Arabica coffee
rose 1.8% to $2.7325 per lb. The market lost 1.8% last week.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
rose 2% to 17.37 cents/lb, after setting a three-month low of 16.82 on Friday.
* Citi on Friday closed its long sugar call position with July expiry SBN7C at a loss of 47 cents, after a stop-loss signal was triggered.
* The bank, however, left its constructive quarterly price outlook unchanged, saying it still expects lower supply from India and potential limits on how much sugar Brazil can export.
* White sugar
was little changed at $487.90 a ton.
COCOA
* London cocoa
​​​slipped 0.4% to £4,079 a ton, having gained 1% last week.
* Cocoa arrivals at ports in top grower Ivory Coast were down 47.1% at 54,000 metric tons in the week ending November 22 versus the same period a year ago, exporters estimated.
* Below-average rain last week in most of Ivory Coast's cocoa-growing regions raised concerns about pod development for the main crop harvest early next year, farmers said.
* New York cocoa
slipped 0.6% to $5,238 a ton.
